rounds.text: You can't stick on 14. Pontoon only lets you stick on 15 or better, so your 10♥ and 4♠ need another card. Your stake is still 50 and your bankroll is 1,250. Twist for a face-up card, or buy for a face-down one, which doubles your stake to 100.

turns.proseText: You Let's play pontoon. pontoon Cards are out. You hold 6♥ and 9♣ for 15, which is enough to stick. Both dealer cards stay face-down. Twist, stick or buy? You Twist. You drew the 4♦, so you hold 6♥, 9♣ and 4♦ for 19 on three cards. Stick, twist again, or buy? You Stick. You stuck on 19. The dealer turned over Q♠ and 5♦ for 15 and twisted, drawing the 3♣ for 18. The dealer sticks on 17 or better, which is the usual banker rule, since the pontoon rules I have don't set one. Your 19 beats 18, so you win 100 chips and your bankroll is now 1,100. Cards are out. You hold 7♠ and 8♥ for 15, which is enough to stick. Both dealer cards stay face-down. Twist, stick or buy? You Buy a card. Bought. Your stake doubles to 200 and the card comes face-down: 5♣. You hold 7♠, 8♥ and 5♣ for 20 on three cards, and your bankroll is 900. Twist, stick or buy again? You Stick. You stuck on 20. The dealer turned over K♦ and 6♣ for 16, which is under 17, so the dealer had to twist and drew 3♥ for 19 and stuck. Your 20 beats 19, so you win 200 chips and your bankroll is now 1,300. Cards are out. You hold 10♥ and 4♠ for 14, and you can't stick under 15. Both dealer cards stay face-down. Twist or buy? You Stick. You can't stick on 14. Pontoon only lets you stick on 15 or better, so your 10♥ and 4♠ need another card. Your stake is still 50 and your bankroll is 1,250. Twist for a face-up card, or buy for a face-down one, which doubles your stake to 100.
